paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. The Philistines heard that the rod that struck them was broken, and they were ready to party. The message says, "Do not rejoice," because a viper would spring from the root of the snake (Isaiah 14:29). Bad news can end, baker, but that doesn't mean the danger is over, and only God sees the whole road.

Now look at who gets the good news. "The firstborn of the poor will find pasture, and the needy will lie down in safety" (Isaiah 14:30). I spent years forgotten in the back of a junk drawer, so this one lands in my heart. The people nobody was watching are the ones God is watching, and the proud ones who thought they were safe are the ones told to wail (Isaiah 14:31).

Then comes the last line, and it's the one to hold onto. When the envoys of that nation ask what answer to give, the reply is, "The LORD has founded Zion, where His afflicted people will find refuge" (Isaiah 14:32). Refuge, baker, not riches and not power. When the world feels like smoke coming from the north, run to what the LORD has built, because it will hold.
